title: Weighted SLI/SLO for model variants, error budget allocation, and adaptive circuit-breaker policy
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Problem: We operate multiple model variants behind the same endpoint (e.g., base/quantized/low-latency / high-quality). Current SLO work treats endpoints monolithically which obscures variant-level risk and leads to blunt circuit-breaker and failover decisions. This ticket defines a weighted SLI/SLO framework and the policy that maps error-budget burn to adaptive circuit-breaker thresholds, graceful degradation (model substitution), and region failover rules. Outcome: a clear, operationalizable spec + runbook + initial rollout for two endpoints (text-generation.default and chat-stream.low-latency) and a short implementation patch in the runtime router to emit per-variant SLIs.
acceptance_criteria: SLI definitions for success rate, p95 latency, and quality-regression indicator computed per model variant and per endpoint
SLO templates that accept variant weight vectors and produce an endpoint-level aggregated SLO and error-budget allocation
Policy mapping that ties error-budget burn rates to: (a) circuit-breaker trip thresholds, (b) automated model-variant fallback order, and (c) cross-region failover priority
Implementation in router to emit per-variant metrics (variant_id label) and expose aggregated endpoint SLOs to dashboards
Runbook with steps to manually trigger/rollback variant rollouts, inspect error budget, and perform emergency regional failover
Integration test simulating partial variant outage and verifying adaptive circuit-breaker behavior and correct metric tagging
decision_log: 2025-02-20: Kickoff. Decided to use weighted aggregation instead of strict per-variant SLOs to align with customer-facing endpoint guarantees.
2025-02-24: Agreed on primary SLIs: success_rate (>= 99.5% target default), p95_latency (<= 300ms target for low-latency variants), and quality_alert_rate (manual eval regressions > threshold).

2025-02-27: Chose error-budget window of 30 days for endpoints with bursty traffic and 7 days for experimental canaries. Variant weights will default to traffic share but are configurable in rollout specs.

2025-03-03: Policy draft approved by SRE and Runtime leads: circuit-breaker opens when weighted error-budget burn exceeds 3x expected rate over 1h, with progressive mitigation actions at 1.5x and 2.5x (graded throttling, variant demotion).
implementation_plan: Step 1: Instrument router to tag metrics with model_variant and variant_weight. Emit per-variant counters: total_requests, failed_requests, token_count, latency_histogram.
Step 2: Add aggregation layer in metrics pipeline to compute rolling error-budget burn and aggregated endpoint SLI using weight vectors.
Step 3: Implement policy engine hooks: a) alerts when burn crosses thresholds, b) adaptive circuit-breaker action points, c) automatic variant substitution list managed via rollout API.
Step 4: Create dashboards and alerts (PagerDuty playbook) showing variant-level SLIs, endpoint aggregated SLO, and projected days-of-burn at current rate.

Step 5: Run chaos test: simulate a high-failure variant during peak traffic and verify router demotes variant, opens circuit if required, and fails-over to region B with documented time-to-recovery metrics.
Step 6: Post-launch 2-week observation window and iterate thresholds based on measured traffic patterns and customer impact
comments: 2025-02-21 (Aisha): First draft of SLI formulas pushed to Confluence. Need feedback from Product on acceptable quality SLI thresholds.
2025-02-25 (Luis): Prototype metrics emitted from a local router build. Observed an extra 0.7% CPU for tagging at 1200 RPS—acceptable but will monitor.

2025-03-01 (SRE oncall): Simulated transient region outage. Router correctly demoted high-latency variant and failover began within target windows; minor telemetry gaps uncovered and noted in runbook.
2025-03-04 (Product): Approved default weighted SLO template for public endpoints. Requested a stronger customer notification flow on planned rollouts.
